 Oklahoma City Thunder at Cleveland Cavaliers NBA Prediction, Picks & Odds for Nov. 2, 2026
 Athlon Sports AI News Desk, Cory Bonini 2026년 11월 2일 월 오후 10:18 UTC 0 (Benny Sieu - Imagn Images) The Cleveland Cavaliers have been on the road for two straight, but on Monday they’ll finally head home. They will face off against the Oklahoma City Thunder at 7 p.m. ET at Rocket Arena. Oklahoma City’s defense has allowed only 107 points per game this season, so Cleveland will have its work cut out on offense.
 Cleveland is coming off its highest-scoring game of the season. The Cavaliers put the hurt on the Milwaukee Bucks with a sharp 136-111 victory on Saturday. The contest was pretty much decided by halftime, when Cleveland held a 72-46 lead.
 The Cavaliers can attribute much of their success to Evan Mobley, who shot 68.8 percent (11-for-16) from the field en route to 27 points and five rebounds, and Jarrett Allen, who posted a double-double with 25 points and 11 rebounds.
 Cleveland was working as a unit and finished the game with 41 assists. The Cavaliers haven’t recorded that many since Feb. 1, when they also had 41 vs. Portland.
 Meanwhile, Oklahoma City took a 119-98 punch to the gut from the Houston Rockets on Saturday, marking its second straight defeat. The Thunder’s loss came despite a quality game from Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who scored 26 points. Jared McCain, on the other hand, was considerably less helpful after going 0-for-5 from deep.
 With Chet Holmgren (knee), Jalen Williams (ankle), and Cason Wallace (shoulder) facing lengthy recoveries, Oklahoma City will rely even more heavily on Gilgeous-Alexander and Isaiah Hartenstein.
 The Cavaliers have been performing well recently, winning four of their last five matchups. That’s helped them to a 4-2 record this season. Cleveland’s offense has played a big role in that success, averaging 124.0 points over those five games. As for the Thunder, they have now lost three of their last four road games. Despite that, they’re 4-2 this season.
 Going forward, the Cavaliers are the favorite in this one, as the oddsmakers expect to see them win by 4.5 points.
 Cleveland couldn’t quite get it done against Oklahoma City in the teams’ most recent meeting on Feb. 22 last season, falling 121-113. Will the Cavaliers have more luck at home instead of on the road?
